steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Industry 4.0: the Fourth Industrial Revolution — cyber-physical systems, IoT, cloud computing and automation transforming manufacturing.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 3D printing (additive manufacturing): builds objects layer by layer from CAD models — rapid prototyping, custom medical implants, reduced waste.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Robotics: automated systems replacing repetitive tasks — increases consistency, reduces labour costs, raises ethical concerns about job losses.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Internet of Things (IoT): everyday objects connected to the internet — smart homes, wearable tech, data-driven design decisions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how 3D printing has changed the prototype development process in product design. | Discuss the social and economic impacts of increasing automation in manufacturing. | Evaluate how the Internet of Things could influence the design of a domestic kettle.

steps.title: Check your answers

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always link technology to a specific product or context — never write about technology in the abstract Consider BOTH benefits AND drawbacks — exam questions often ask you to evaluate Use precise terminology: 'additive manufacturing' not just '3D printing' for higher marks
